learning_outcomes.text: Knows the methodology for developing technical and scientific projects and academic writing standards.
Understands the design and operating principles of automotive propulsion systems (thermal, hybrid, electric).
Knows CAD modeling, CAE simulation methods, and manufacturing technologies applicable in the automotive industry.
Understands technical regulations, quality standards, and PSI norms applicable to the field.
Correctly defines the project topic and establishes technical and functional objectives.
Performs 3D modeling and necessary analyses for validating constructive solutions.
Uses specialized software for design, simulation, and technical documentation.
Develops complete project documentation, including calculations, drawings, technological plans, and economic analyses.
Plans and autonomously manages project stages, respecting deadlines and quality requirements.
Respects academic integrity norms, professional ethics, and occupational safety.
Collaborates effectively with the supervisor and industrial partners, communicating clearly and professionally.
Self-evaluates progress and adopts measures for improving results.

syllabus_topics: Plagiarism check, re-correction. Presentation of the work, answers to questions
teaching_methods: Thematic workshops for CAD/CAE software usage
Independent work based on a work plan
Use of digital resources and specialized laboratories
Progress monitored through intermediate presentations and formative evaluations
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits.
